prompt:
Rachel still hasn't come back on Mina's final offer. It's been about a week, her board should've happened, and I'm not authorizing a chase. CE doesn't go back in blind. Before anyone touches Vectral, pull the real picture from our systems, not Slack: deal status, anything from Rachel since the nineteenth, whether the client record still matches, whether the platform issues she escalated are closed in tracking or still open, stipend mess since the audit, real open AR versus estimates, and moves still in flight. If CRM, email, billing, and ops don't line up, say so.

Same pass on NorthWind, BrightLoop, Mosaic, StormCloud, and Terraform Digital. Only flag where the systems materially disagree. While you're in it, catch me up on the four calls warping Vectral posture: Chloe and David's BrightLoop temp-coordinator ask, Terraform coordinator capacity after the hire I signaled, Marcus on the vendor strategy memo, and whether the June DOT package still has placarding or cert gaps vendors only covered verbally.

Then document the posture. No outreach to Rachel. Keep the renewal at risk; CRM note on the hold and what's still live on ExpenseBot, stipends, billing, and active moves. Same on the other five with honest status and next steps; move both open NorthWind Denver expansion deals to at-risk and leave closed-won alone. Comment still-open ExpenseBot remediation tickets, Marcus's vendor memo workstream, and outstanding DOT work. Brief David and Mina on the hold and what CE needs if Rachel reaches out first; Marcus on finance/vendor/billing/compliance and what's blocking his memo; Samira on whether engineering is still in Rachel's way; Chloe on capacity and the staffing answer I still owe her. Short #executive readout: hold, isolated or pattern, which accounts matter, what's still on me. Don't dress it up if the records are messy.
